newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares gain 2.71 pct in cautious trade.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares gain 2.71 pct in cautious trade.

text.p: Istanbul shares rose an average 2.71 percent on Friday in a mild recovery that followed Thursday's 4.49 percent plunge, but the market remained cautious amid persisting political concerns, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed 41 points, or 2.71 percent higher at 1,552. It was up 2.25 percent in the morning.
Over the week, the index lost 6.2 percent after last week's 10.34 percent surge caused by easing political tension and privatisation expectations.
Trade volume dropped to 21.83 trillion lira from Thursday's 27.51 trillion.
"Some players bought ahead of Monday's MGK (National Security Council) meeting and others maintained their positions," said Serdar Karatepe from Polen securities.

Political fears mounted earlier this week due to the ruling Islamist Welfare Party's opposition to a plan to raise compulsory education to eight years from five as part of measures put forward at the military-dominated MGK's February 28 meeting to combat rising Islamist activism.
Several brokers expect the index to drift between 1,500 support and 1,600 resistance next week under the shadow of politics. The market focuses primarily on Monday's MGK meeting.

Of the 238 shares traded, rises outdid fallsy by 121 to 47 and 70 closed steady. The IMKB Industrial gained 1.57 percent to 1,553, the IMKB Services firmed 0.51 percent to 1,392 and the IMKB Financial leapt 4.64 percent to 1,692.

Top actives were T.Isbank's C series, up 1,000 lira at 47,000, state oil refiner Tupras, up 3,00 lira at 63,000, utility Cukurova Elektrik, steady at 197,500 lira and ground handling firm Celebi, up 9,000 lira at 77,000. They made up 23 percent of the total turnover.
